As she saw how the buildings thrust through the clouds and towered in the skies, what filled the mind of the Zalak girl, not yet Flametail Knight, was the loftiest red pine back home.
And they hit her heart—a flash of longing, a flash of depression—as she recalled that final swathe of Pinus Sylvestris still standing, only to be razed in a sudden Catastrophe.
Sona had never actually returned to that forest since.
Perhaps that pine was lucky enough to survive the disaster? And maybe, some time next year, the pinecones that fell intact would find a completely new life in the ash-blanketed earth... just as she did.
She had to live on, in the stead of her friends and family who lost their lives to Catastrophe. She had to plant roots and bud in the soil they named Kazimierz. Such notions kept her driven to the present day.
But before she knew it, Sona was shaking her head free of them all. They skipped too many steps—they would only trap her in more regrettable circumstances. She couldn't go on like this. She had to learn to be optimistic. Shape up her act, and perhaps the merchants would give her an out, and employ this little Infected girl to do what handiwork she could.
Soon after, she learned from newspapers and television that Infected, too, could be knights. She was going to find a way in. Still, she wanted to become one just so she could make a living. With no chivalric spirit of old turned life lesson, and no grand visions or hopes, Sona clenched her fist tight.
But the next thing she knew, she was being forced to raise it against fellow Infected who deserved it just as little.
Sona wasn't strong, but she was nimble. She stood out amongst the Infected for it, and was selected by the bankroller of an underground power and sent into the 'cleaning qualifiers.' No weapon in hand, danger surrounding her, and a single fist planted in her foe's face. And they toppled, and Sona won the right to survive another day—but she wasn't happy. She wasn't strong. Taking her opponent down in one blow... it could only be because they were starving, because the evening before, their backer 'tipped' a few knights some bonds to get into a brawl with them.
Sona wasn't happy. She wasn't strong.
Some fawned, telling her if she just dressed up a little, she'd be so cute, so lovely and sweet. Some gushed, telling her if she just went through some proper training, she'd be a terror of the racetrack.
Until one voice told her: 'You've got a tail like a blazing fire.' It caught her off guard.
There was nothing in particular beneath that statement, and it was no more than an ordinary spectator, reveling in the violence, who yelled it.
But it was the first time Sona had ever choked with emotion after a match.
Yes. She'd just realized it. She ought to be like a blazing fire.
uniequip_002_vigil:
The shoe-shiner trembles as he enters the Bellone famiglia parlor.
He trembles not because this is Bellone territory. He had shined Bernardo's shoes for thirty years, and the man always respected those who respected him. The last time he had stepped into this parlor, it was so that he could offer Bernardo the chance to name his son.
His fear comes from the fact that the one sitting here today is not Bernardo, but his son, Leontuzzo.
He has not heard much about the Bellone heir. All he knew was that the young master had never come to him for a shoe shining.
'My father isn't here at the moment, but you can trust me as you trusted him.'
His words calm him a bit, allowing the shoe-shiner to explain why he had no choice but to come:
His son leads a decent, honorable life, and fell in love with a lady from Columbia. However, that lady was also being pursued by a maniac who didn't take kindly to a rival. Three nights ago, his son was cornered by that maniac and beaten within an inch of his life. He'd sought aid from the courts, but the man belonged to a Columbian famiglia, and his lawyers were easily able to secure a 'not guilty.'
'When I was leaving the courtroom, he stepped in front of me and shoved two banknotes into my pocket. He laughed as he told me it was for my son's medical fees. I...' The shoe-shiner went on, tears streaming from his wizened eyes.
Leontuzzo listens in silence. He knows that if his father were here, he would surely give the old man a pat on the shoulder, acknowledge his suffering, then provide a solution to this. A humane way.
Generally speaking, these things could only be resolved with bloodshed.
But that was not how he does things.
'What is it you wish for, signor?'
'I have no requests, Don Leontuzzo, other than justice for my boy.'
'Justice. Am I to understand that you want this man to feel the same pain your son did?'
'That's right. Nothing more.'
Leontuzzo snaps his fingers, and a red-headed young man steps out from a door to the side.
'Demetri, go investigate the gang behind that guy first.'
'Easy enough, but what comes next?'
'Next... If I'm not mistaken, those Columbian gangs want to sidestep us and cozy up to the local government. Then let's propose sending local 'talents' to the Columbian frontier. Hopefully, every famiglia will enthusiastically agree. Let them send off a few stronzi who should have been exiled long ago.'
The red-headed youth snaps his fingers. 'So we'll ship this guy off too?'
'Exactly.'
'Capisco.'
With that final declaration, the man leaves the room. Leontuzzo turns towards the astonished shoe-shiner. 'This is the justice I can give you. Are you satisfied with it, signor?'
The shoe-shiner quickly catches on, and his gaze turns from astonishment to gratitude.
'Take this.'
'This is...'
'My pistola. Place it by your shoe-shiner, and nobody will cause you trouble.'
'But—'
'Don't worry. I barely use it. Whenever you feel like you can sleep easy again, just give it back to the guard downstairs.'
uniequip_003_vigil:
Leontuzzo is somewhat nervous in the driver's seat. Today is the first time he's officially driving a car.
Look both ways. Adjust the seat. Adjust the rear-view mirror. Fasten the seatbelt. Check the gear. Once all these steps are complete, he looks at the passenger seat with some trepidation. Lavinia sits there, his instructor for the day. Only once she nods does he let out a faint sigh of relief, turn the key, and start the engine. The car slowly trundles out the garage and onto the street.
The streets are, as always, showered in a patter of drizzle. Leontuzzo flicks the windshield wipers, taking care to keep his foot on the brake, and not daring to go too fast.
'You're driving far too slowly, Leon. You'll never learn anything like that.' Her role as driving instructor has not given her cause to loosen her usual strictness.
'The more you remind me, the more nervous I get, Lavinia.' Leontuzzo has a death grip on the steering wheel, his eyes locked onto the road ahead, refusing to turn his head even an inch.
'Who was it at breakfast who was so excited to show off his skills to Demetri once he got back?'
'I let the steam from the bread get to my head.'
As they speak, the car reaches an intersection. Just as the red lights are about to go green, several pedestrians cross. However, the moment they see the emblem atop the oncoming car, they immediately lower their heads and hurry down the rest of the crosswalk.
Unfortunately for one of them, they trip and fall as they do so.
Lavinia looks at Leontuzzo, as if asking him: 'What should you do in this situation?'
'...I should slam the accelerator and run the red light. Best to give them a splash and a little scare.'
But even as he says this, he presses down on the brake, letting the car slowly come to a stop in front of the crosswalk.
The fallen pedestrian clambers back to their feet, giving the two in the car a slight nod of thanks before quickly leaving the scene.
'If most famiglia members drove like you, I'd be able to shave off a tenth of the cases I preside over each year, if only for minor incidents like just now.' Lavinia speaks with approval of his action.
'Honestly, there are simply too many traffic laws. I'm not keen on remembering them all either.' The light turns green, and Leontuzzo restarts the car. 'But there's one thing I've come to realize lately. We follow these so-called laws not because they are natural to us, but because they are self-evident principles we as a people discover as we seek justice.'
'Well said, Leon. It seems you have a thorough understanding of those traffic laws after all. Now let's see if you can actually remember them.'
'Oddio, Lavinia, are you seriously going to give a lecture here?'
'I did promise your father to teach you everything I know. So, Leon, what are those white lines by the side of the car meant to indicate?'
'Wait, give me some time to think...'
The rains of Siracusa are endless and suffocating, but at the very least, inside this car, the warmth of chatter can be felt.
uniequip_002_mlyss:
In the early morning, long before the staff of the Ecological Section have come to work, a figure strolls through the vivarium. The vents have just opened, and the entire place quickly fills with mist. The figure remains at ease, briskly skipping about from plant to plant, occasionally tapping at the terminal on her chest before drifting to the next. After a full round, she chucks her terminal into a meeting room with a resounding 'clack' that fades away into nothingness.

By the break of dawn, a line is already forming before a Trimounts bakery. Though most researchers care about meals only insofar as they fill stomachs and provide nutrition, inevitably a few would prefer to savor their food and drink. She is also in that line, hoping for freshly-baked bread and especially this bakery's salt-crust loaves. She glances at the queue in front of her, then at the big clock across the street. She then calculates how much longer it would take to have her fill of delicious bread...

Muelsyse sits at the dresser, looking at her Dresser Flowing Shape while combing her hair.
She has an Ecological internal meeting to attend in half an hour, but there is nary not a hint of worry on her face.
Her Dresser Flowing Shape acts as a mirror and follows along with her movements. Occasionally, it decides to be a bit impish and changes its posture, to the consternation of its master as she tries to put on her makeup.
After tying up her hair for the day and putting on whatever jewelry she feels like, Muelsyse flings her chapstick into her pocket before giving a wave to her Dresser Flowing Shape, which reverts to a fountain.
Upon opening the door to her room, she sees some bread atop the table, along with a salad and some water.

She enters Ecological, a gaggle of researchers surrounds her as she walks towards the meeting room. Newcomers are amazed that the director doesn't even need to glance at her notes before immediately going into presentation mode, while veterans have long since gotten used to this.
After all, she is their director, predicting her actions is like trying to catch the wind.
As such, almost none of them could imagine that at this very moment—
She is in the vivarium, looking at a dewdrop form on the tip of a leaf.
She is by a fountain in a city park, feeding the fowlbeasts.
She is in the fountain on her dresser, where she continues to sleep.
She is—

'I'm here, drinking coffee with you aboard Rhodes Island.
'Pretty amazing, right?'
After seeing Muelsyse cross her arms and lift her head with pride, you hurriedly agree. You've seen her impressive abilities up close, although you have noticed a few... oddities in the small details—
You've seen her press the wrong button on her terminal, forcing the vivarium staff to take cover from the sudden rain.
You've seen her curiously take a bite of the feed in the park while feeding the fowlbeasts.
You've even seen her draw an arc across her chin with chapstick.
Skilled technicians controlling multiple terminals are bound to make mistakes, so it's only natural that Muelsyse would have trouble with multiple Dresser Flowing Shapes, right?
But when you recall the sight of her stirring the air above her coffee cup, you can't help but laugh.
As a result, and rightfully so, you suffer a one-two punch from Muelsyse's Dresser Flowing Shape.
uniequip_003_mlyss:
Carrying a cute umbrella is the best way to start a conversation.
People will ask about your leaf umbrella, turn the topic to themselves, sigh about how the seasons change, and how spring will eventually come. They always skip winter, and end the conversation on a positive note. Finally, you enjoy a dance with them. The dance is mandatory for new meetings. Many relationships begin with a dance, and Muelsyse never misses the opportunity for one.
But does she really need these 'opportunities' from those so-called 'networking' sessions?
The question is like a stone failing to skip across a pond. It falls into the water with a dull splash and sinks for eternity.
She changes one dance partner for another, and then another, her steps growing ever more graceful. Muelsyse once thought she could master every dance there was. She also once thought she had many 'friends' by her side. Until Kristen and Saria showed up.
The silent stone beneath the water became a pea under her mattress. Hidden for a so long, it finally got to shout out loud: Hey? Was that really what's been happening? Subvert your own expectations, and see what's true or false! It's time for fate to bring you some real 'like-minded' people!
It was a meeting arranged by her supervisor, with only two other people from a small laboratory.
We all know how it ended. The lab of two became a lab of three, and she was the first to join. Boom, 'Rhine Lab' was founded.
'No, no, no, this isn't right...' She had just finished writing her final thesis and had gone without a night of proper sleep for two weeks. She slumped over the table, '...We should try this method first, it has a higher chance of success!'
'This is why it's good to have a group of three. Let's take a vote.' Kristen from the other side of the table takes another sip of coffee, dark circles around her eyes. Saria nods silently.
'So, hands up if you agree with plan A.'
Kristen raises her hand, and so does Saria. A frown slides onto Muelsyse's weary face.
'Ugh... h-hands up if you're with plan B!' She raises her hand, her lonely arm standing aloft.
Immediately after, amid the sound of water, another hand raises. Followed by a second, and a third. The identical water clones look at their two companions, and the elf grins: 'Hehe, four to two, how 'bout that?'
'It's not fair...'
'Four to two, fair enough, no? This Muelsyse, that Muelsyse, and that Muelsyse are all members of Rhine Lab. They have the right to vote too.'
A reasonable point. A group of reasonable friends. Seems strange, but this is how those from Rhine Lab joke around. As for what came next, how the victorious water clones cheered in unison and spilled coffee onto Kristen's beautiful trench coat... we'll get back to that next time.
Amidst the shrieks and sorries, Muelsyse hears something. A quiet, subtle, moist, sound. A sprout emerging from the soil.
It was that pea—it had found the soil. It began to take root and sprout.
The seasons change, and spring will always come.
uniequip_002_ines:
Only three in the afternoon, and the sunlight has already stopped shining on the little store. In the gloom, Ines sweeps the last of the broken glass down the steps, then heads back into the shop to sit down. The general store is located halfway up a slope. Anyone who passes by will see it and its bizarre one-and-a-half-step stairs.
The place was chosen by Hoederer, who said it was prime real estate and that she'd make her money back quick, but she originally just wanted to go find a container out in the sheds that didn't leak, dump her 'goods' inside, and collect the money at the door, like back in the Scar Market days. But she didn't argue. The war was over, for now, and the people returning to Kazdel should also return to their former lives. A proper place to buy things was only the first step.
'You put the curtain away?' Hoederer had tried to lift it out of habit as he walked in.
A finger extends out of the shadows, pointing at the ornamental fin bowl on the counter. Multicolored beads from the curtain line its bottom, but there is no fin there, nor any water.
'...It's fine. As long as the beads are still here, I can string them back together.'
The finger retracts back into the shadows. Hoederer walks to the shelves, picking up the fallen Originium bomb samples one by one and placing them back into their box, then moves on to tidying up the knives. Everything else, he reorganizes by how dangerous they are and where they were imported from. Once done, he gives it all a once-over. A damp, sticky liquid remains on the floor, the result of someone giving up trying to clean it halfway through.
The man walks back to the counter and pulls out a very fortunate three-legged stool to sit on. From his pockets, he takes out a knife and a piece of wood the size of his hand. By the time Ines finally pulls herself out of her contemplation, he has carved it into an oval.
'What're you doing?'
'I call it the 'W-tato'. Doesn't it look like her?'
'Not in the slightest. And you know that's wood, right?'
'Right, because real potatoes should be for eating.'
'And real knives should be for killing.'
'Was that what you were thinking when you used that real knife of yours to carve your horns?'
Ines sinks back into silence. Hoederer blows away the wood shavings. To his surprise, there is a faint glimmer accompanying them as they flutter through the air.
'Alright, change of topic. What happened earlier?'
'Some people decided this place was their safehouse and storeroom. I corrected them, that's all.'
'And that liquid on the ground...?'
'Soda.'
'Did they repay you?'
The woman gives him a look that all but says 'Are you serious?'. Hoederer puts down the W-tato and gropes around in the drawer, pulling out the account book from its depths.
'Ones, tens, hundreds, thousands, ten thousands... That's a lot of zeros, Ines. You sure you wrote this down right?'
'Look where the decimal point is.'
'......
'I'll be honest, I don't think you should be keeping your accounts like this.'
'The numbers aren't wrong.'
'No, that's not... fine. At least the bowl didn't break, right? And no blood was shed. I think you can move the decimal point forward a spot—'
'It was just a bunch of kids who got duped into coming here. They couldn't even tell the bombs from the soda bottles. They just grab the box and ran.
'I tripped them up, but one of them knocked over a shelf, giving the other two a chance to escape.'
'You went easy on them.'
'I was busy saving the fin and its bowl.'
'You can always buy another fin... Going to open up shop tomorrow?'
Ines steps out of the darkness onto the damp spot, looking all around her.
'Of course, why wouldn't I?
'The shop's already here.'
uniequip_002_grani:
Ever since she obtained this mounted police badge, Grani's been waiting for this day. Not looking for a wallet, not unlocking a door for a citizen who forgot their keys. Today, she's finally gotten an official assignment, doing something the mounted police should do—she's joining in the escort of a criminal.
'Uhh! Not that I'm saying unlocking things isn't what a police officer should do... just...'
It's just that she finally gets to do something she's dreamt of since the beginning.

'We've been attacked by an armed group, and we're low on heads! Division Three requesting backup!'
'How are you, Division Two? Send two for emergency support! Hold on until HQ get here!'
'It's Grani's team... She shouldn't be taking assignments like this...'
The fleet transporting the convict come to an emergency stop under the sudden attack, and though they're prepared for this, the numbers they're facing still exceed the mounted police's expectations.
Grani holds a defensive posture behind the escort vehicles, the convict still inside, held by a teammate—they're not letting the door open again under any circumstances, as per code, so no worries about the subject.
After that comes devoting everything to prolong the ceasefire as long as possible, waiting for support.
But her superior's words just now get Grani a little mad. She's heard words to that effect more than enough times, yes, but today's her first time on an official assignment, and she thought that was recognition of her ability.
...Guess it wasn't.

'All you need to do is stay here and defend the vehicle, and wait for us to sort this out.'
Grani watches her two seniors run in armed against their fire, and they take down one, two... even more of the enemy appears from behind the bunker, shouting 'There's only two of them!' and rushing... her seniors and teammates suddenly fall, they pull their hands from the wounds they were clutching, and Grani sees palms red with blood.
The parked fleet creating its own highly useful bunker, Grani conceals within it and launches charge after charge. Her teammates have lost hope until they see her routing the enemy's formation, and they're hauled back into safety one after another by this pint-sized girl. The opposition so much as beats a retreat for the time being.

......
The support squads following up take over the task of escorting the convict, and Grani keeps her injured seniors and teammates company on the way to a nearby hospital for treatment.
Bit by bit, she's been changing the way people see her, and though she's never rejected herself, getting the recognition of others is something that pleases her all the same.
Grani dusts off the badge on her shoulder, a bit of ash stuck to it from the conflict before, and now it glimmers bright.
